image.subject: a steep narrow timber staircase inside a seventeenth-century house, worn treads, a dim window at the top

storyboard.claim: Henry's point: the stairs were built for human efficiency, not to stop ghosts
storyboard.concreteVisual: the cramped steep staircase, its treads worn narrow, climbing into dimness
storyboard.relationToPrevious: opens the stair argument for the first time in this stretch
storyboard.addedInformation: the stairs are a working tool of the house, not a spiritual barrier

image.subject: a plain dark wooden hallway of the house, one candle on a shelf, nothing supernatural in the shadows

storyboard.claim: the terror in Peton is practical, not spectral
storyboard.concreteVisual: an ordinary hallway with one candle and empty shadows
storyboard.relationToPrevious: follows the stairs with the plain reason they exist
storyboard.addedInformation: the fear is of people, not of anything in the walls

image.subject: a dark attic under sloping timber rafters, a gap between the floorboards letting in faint light, a crouched human shape far back in the shadows

storyboard.claim: the real threat is living people hiding in the attic
storyboard.concreteVisual: the attic with a crouched human shape in the far dark
storyboard.relationToPrevious: turns the stair point into the attic's occupant
storyboard.addedInformation: someone is up there, alive, hiding

image.subject: from a dark attic, a person peers down through a slatted gap in the floorboards onto a candlelit room below, a table and a chair in the lamplight

storyboard.claim: the attic lets someone spy on the lower floors unseen
storyboard.concreteVisual: a watcher looking down through a floor gap at a lit room
storyboard.relationToPrevious: shows the hiding figure watching the rooms below
storyboard.addedInformation: the attic is a hidden observation post over the household

storyboard.claim: the threat moves from the ethereal to the visceral
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a reaction line with no picture needed
storyboard.relationToPrevious: reacts to the human-threat idea
storyboard.addedInformation: a fight against a person is a fight you can win

storyboard.claim: people built the cramped stairs to hide, which flips the protection idea
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, spoken reasoning only
storyboard.relationToPrevious: reframes the stairs once more as human construction
storyboard.addedInformation: the stairs were never a magical barrier protecting the family

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, edging through a narrow hidden passage between timber walls, a candle in her hand

storyboard.claim: the house is a structure where the living move through hidden passages like vermin
storyboard.concreteVisual: a woman sliding through a cramped gap between timber walls
storyboard.relationToPrevious: puts a person inside the wall passages
storyboard.addedInformation: the passages are used by the living to move unseen

image.subject: an old yellowed household ledger open on a wooden table, handwritten columns of names and debts, a quill pen beside it

storyboard.claim: the house keeps the physical evidence of every lie told inside it
storyboard.concreteVisual: an open household ledger with handwritten columns
storyboard.relationToPrevious: moves from the walls to the paper record the house keeps
storyboard.addedInformation: the house holds written proof, not only hidden rooms

image.subject: the heavy chestnut front door of a timber house set into a dark wall at dusk, a lantern beside the threshold

storyboard.claim: the dread starts at the house's threshold
storyboard.concreteVisual: the front door at dusk with a lantern at its edge
storyboard.relationToPrevious: leaves the interior and moves to the door
storyboard.addedInformation: the boundary of the house is where the dread begins

storyboard.claim: the boundary between the wild and the house
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a continuing sentence
storyboard.relationToPrevious: finishes the threshold sentence
storyboard.addedInformation: the house stands on the edge of the wild

image.subject: a muddy 1692 village street of timber houses at dusk, townspeople in dark wool cloaks standing in small wary groups

storyboard.claim: 1692 colony atmosphere is suffocating
storyboard.concreteVisual: a muddy village street at dusk with wary townspeople
storyboard.relationToPrevious: jumps from the threshold to the 1692 town
storyboard.addedInformation: the village is suspicious and tense

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, running down a muddy village street at dusk and looking back over her shoulder

storyboard.claim: Caroline is terrified after an encounter in town
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline running down a muddy street, looking back in fear
storyboard.relationToPrevious: introduces Caroline in the town street
storyboard.addedInformation: she has just met the killer and is running from him

image.subject: dense dark woods at night, undergrowth trampled flat, a pale strip of cloth caught on a low branch

storyboard.claim: Jonas Reev is the killer roaming the woods
storyboard.concreteVisual: trampled woods at night with a torn cloth on a branch
storyboard.relationToPrevious: places the killer's hunting ground in the woods
storyboard.addedInformation: the killer leaves a trail of disturbed brush

image.subject: a dark woodland path at dawn, footprints in the mud leading into the brush

storyboard.claim: the killer is huge and has already claimed four lives
storyboard.concreteVisual: footprints leading off a woodland path into the brush
storyboard.relationToPrevious: shows the aftermath of his hunting
storyboard.addedInformation: his size and his tracks are the evidence

image.subject: four small plain wooden grave markers in a woodland clearing, half hidden in leaves

storyboard.claim: four victims left in the brush, he is a monster
storyboard.concreteVisual: four plain grave markers in a clearing
storyboard.relationToPrevious: shows the four victims the narration counts
storyboard.addedInformation: the dead were left in the woods

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, running up a muddy path toward a timber house with lit windows

storyboard.claim: Caroline runs back to Peton and sees it as an impenetrable fortress
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline running toward the lit house on its path
storyboard.relationToPrevious: sends Caroline from the woods to the house
storyboard.addedInformation: the house is her refuge in her mind

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, pushing a heavy iron bolt across a massive chestnut door

storyboard.claim: Caroline bolts the huge chestnut door
storyboard.concreteVisual: her hands on a heavy iron bolt across the chestnut door
storyboard.relationToPrevious: she arrives and seals the door
storyboard.addedInformation: the door is massive, a physical lock against the outside

image.subject: close-up of a heavy black iron bear knocker on a chestnut door, its jaws wide open, iron teeth bared

storyboard.claim: the knocker is a snarling iron bear made in England
storyboard.concreteVisual: the iron bear knocker with open jaws and bared teeth
storyboard.relationToPrevious: she fixates on the knocker outside the door
storyboard.addedInformation: the bear's form is snarling and fierce

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, turning her head to look back over her shoulder at a dark doorway, frightened eyes

storyboard.claim: Caroline feels a killer's gaze on her back
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline glancing back at a dark doorway
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the knocker moves her attention to the imagined gaze
storyboard.addedInformation: she feels watched from outside

left.label: GUARDIAN
left.subject: the heavy iron bear knocker on a chestnut door, lit warmly from inside by candlelight

right.label: KILLER
right.subject: dark woods at night beyond an iron gate, nothing visible but black trees

storyboard.claim: the bear is her guardian while the killer is outside
storyboard.concreteVisual: the bear knocker against the dark woods
storyboard.relationToPrevious: sets the bear against the killer in the woods
storyboard.addedInformation: the bear is read as protection against the woods

image.subject: a plain 1692 village at night, no lamps lit, a single wooden house door shut tight

storyboard.claim: with no police or alarms, the big door is the only security
storyboard.concreteVisual: a dark village with one shut wooden door
storyboard.relationToPrevious: explains why the door matters in that world
storyboard.addedInformation: there is no other protection in the era

image.subject: a modern suburban front door shut tight at night, a porch light on, a deadbolt visible

storyboard.claim: the door is the only thing between you and death
storyboard.concreteVisual: a modern front door with porch light and deadbolt
storyboard.relationToPrevious: turns the 1692 door toward the present-day viewer
storyboard.addedInformation: the same trust in a door still applies today

image.subject: a tall wooden privacy fence around a suburban backyard at dusk, a porch light on in the house beside it

storyboard.claim: we equate property boundaries with absolute safety
storyboard.concreteVisual: a tall privacy fence around a backyard at dusk
storyboard.relationToPrevious: moves from the door to the fence we build today
storyboard.addedInformation: modern boundaries are the same assumption of safety

storyboard.claim: we buy fences, steel doors and loud cameras to stop the outside world
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a list of protective purchases
storyboard.onScreenText: PRIVACY FENCE / STEEL DOOR / FLOOD LIGHTS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: lists the modern versions of the bear door
storyboard.addedInformation: the list shows how far we go to keep danger outside

image.subject: a suburban front lawn at dusk, a closed gate and a tall fence, a house lit warmly behind it

storyboard.claim: we believe evil stops at our property line
storyboard.concreteVisual: a closed gate and fence at the edge of a lit lawn
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the list leads to the property line
storyboard.addedInformation: we treat the home as sacred and immune

image.subject: an iron key turning in a heavy lock on a timber door, dim candlelight behind it

storyboard.claim: the lock keeps danger out, and the illusion echoes through time
storyboard.concreteVisual: a key turning in a heavy timber-door lock
storyboard.relationToPrevious: sets the lock as the illusion that lasts across centuries
storyboard.addedInformation: the same illusion links the past door to the present one

image.subject: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, standing before a massive chestnut door and looking up at an iron bear knocker

storyboard.claim: Julia as a child was terrified of the same bear knocker
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia looking up at the bear knocker with unease
storyboard.relationToPrevious: jumps to the modern timeline and Julia
storyboard.addedInformation: the fear of the knocker is passed to Julia

left.label: CAROLINE
left.subject: a dim period hallway with a candle in a holder, no people

right.label: JULIA
right.subject: a heavy iron bear knocker on a chestnut door, no people

storyboard.claim: Caroline saw the bear as protector, Julia as monster
storyboard.concreteVisual: two women facing the same knocker, one calm, one afraid
storyboard.relationToPrevious: sets the two women side by side with the knocker
storyboard.addedInformation: the same object reads two ways across the centuries

storyboard.claim: young Julia thought the bear would leap and eat her
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a childhood fear described in speech
storyboard.relationToPrevious: continues Julia's childhood fear
storyboard.addedInformation: the fear was of the bear itself, not the door

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, seated by a fire inside a candlelit room, hands folded in her lap, a steaming bowl of pottage on the table beside her

storyboard.claim: Caroline feels safe inside the house
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline seated by the fire with a bowl of pottage
storyboard.relationToPrevious: turns from Julia back to Caroline's feeling of safety
storyboard.addedInformation: her sense of safety has a reason behind it

storyboard.claim: the bear represents patriarchal protection by men
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, an interpretive claim in speech
storyboard.relationToPrevious: offers a reading of Caroline's safety
storyboard.addedInformation: protection is framed as male authority

image.subject: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, standing in the doorway of a timber house

storyboard.claim: Archie Eldridge is wealthy, powerful and fifteen years older than Caroline
storyboard.concreteVisual: Archie in his dark coat and white collar at the house door
storyboard.relationToPrevious: introduces Archie as the husband behind the protection
storyboard.addedInformation: he built the town's economy and clothes his wife

image.subject: a candlelit table with a steaming bowl of bean pottage and a roaring fire in a stone hearth

storyboard.claim: Archie provides food, clothes and warmth
storyboard.concreteVisual: a steaming pottage bowl and a roaring hearth
storyboard.relationToPrevious: lists what Archie provides
storyboard.addedInformation: the provision is material, the home is well supplied

left.label: WEALTH
left.subject: the heavy iron bear knocker on a gleaming chestnut door

right.label: STATUS
right.subject: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, standing before the same chestnut door

storyboard.claim: the bear is the literal manifestation of Archie's wealth and status
storyboard.concreteVisual: the knocker and Archie standing before the same door
storyboard.relationToPrevious: ties the bear to Archie's status
storyboard.addedInformation: the bear is a symbol of the husband's power

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, standing behind a heavy chestnut door, a dark forest visible through a gap

storyboard.claim: Archie guards his vulnerable wife from the wild woods
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline inside the door with the dark forest beyond the gap
storyboard.relationToPrevious: puts Caroline between the house and the woods
storyboard.addedInformation: the wife is kept inside, away from the wilderness

storyboard.claim: a challenge to the protective reading of the bear
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a question asked in speech
storyboard.relationToPrevious: responds to the protection claim with doubt
storyboard.addedInformation: the reading is disputed

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house at dusk, its heavy door framed like a gaping mouth

storyboard.claim: the bear is the house itself, and the child had the right instinct
storyboard.concreteVisual: the timber house at dusk with its door like an open mouth
storyboard.relationToPrevious: reads the bear as the house Julia reacted to
storyboard.addedInformation: the house itself is the predator

image.subject: a dim upstairs bedroom in a timber house, small leaded windows, a woman's shadow on the wall behind a closed shutter

storyboard.claim: the house devours the women and traps them within its walls
storyboard.concreteVisual: a dim bedroom with a shadow behind a closed shutter
storyboard.relationToPrevious: shows the trap inside the house
storyboard.addedInformation: the women are confined in the rooms

image.subject: the street-facing side of a chestnut door under an iron bear knocker, its teeth pointed toward a dark road

storyboard.claim: the knocker faces the street, so how can it jail?
storyboard.concreteVisual: the knocker on the street side, teeth toward the road
storyboard.relationToPrevious: raises the objection about the bear facing outward
storyboard.addedInformation: the iron faces the street, not the woods

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, standing at a small window looking out at the dark grounds

storyboard.claim: the house forces Caroline to endure what she endures
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline at a small window looking into the dark
storyboard.relationToPrevious: answers the objection with Caroline's experience
storyboard.addedInformation: she is looking outward but the house keeps her in

image.subject: a timber house standing alone on a dark estate, a lone path leading away, distant village lights far off

storyboard.claim: the house isolates her from the community
storyboard.concreteVisual: a lone house on a dark estate with distant village lights
storyboard.relationToPrevious: explains the isolation Caroline feels
storyboard.addedInformation: the community is far away and cut off

storyboard.claim: the domestic dynamic with Archie is toxic and ends in her execution
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a sober verdict in speech
storyboard.relationToPrevious: draws the consequence of the isolation
storyboard.addedInformation: the marriage leads to her death

image.subject: a heavy chestnut door with a large iron padlock hung on its outside hasp, the bear knocker above it

storyboard.claim: the door stops her from leaving, the bear is a padlock on a cell
storyboard.concreteVisual: a padlock on the outside hasp of the chestnut door
storyboard.relationToPrevious: closes the argument with the padlock image
storyboard.addedInformation: the bear is a lock, not a guard dog
